correctness.rationale: A minimal absent factor not among the explicit periodic local types must itself occur in the infinite periodic word, have length >=(k−1)p+2, and have unique-phase prefix/suffix. Their mandatory endpoint occurrences force a border of P^k of length at most (k−1)p, hence exactly the sole terminal obstruction. Disjointness and length enumerator follow. Direct literal-factor set comparison agrees in 147 exhaustive parameter families and 2,104 words; finite data are corroboration, not proof.

value.rationale: Canonical antidictionaries capture the complete negative contiguous-factor information of a string. The theorem gives a uniform closed complete list and length profile over arbitrary alphabets and run-length vectors, and proves a non-obvious stability under arbitrarily many added copies: all but one obstruction remain fixed while one boundary word grows. This sharp circular-versus-finite boundary law is useful to understand compressed repeated texts and is not merely a finite census.
